projects.title: MakeProps
projects.subtitle: Full-stack Developer
projects.description: Independently developed REST APIs and front-end applications for several client projects, covering a range of technical requirements from server-side rendering to graph-database modelling.
projects.problems: The client needed high-performance, search-friendly applications, which led to the use of server-side rendering. Some use cases also required graph data modelling where a conventional relational database had reached its limits.
projects.context: Developed complete web applications with 90% autonomy and occasional reviews from my mentor. Worked across the entire technical stack: back end, databases, front end and production deployment.
highlights: Worked with two back-end stacks (PHP and Node.js) depending on project needs
Implemented SSR with React Router to meet SEO and performance requirements
Used Neo4j alongside PostgreSQL for use cases suited to graph data
Contributed to database design and modelling
Deployed applications to production

projects.title: Hyperfiction
projects.subtitle: C# / Unity Developer
projects.description: Designed and developed three educational XR applications (PC/VR) in C# and Unity for the construction and industrial sectors, including two delivered entirely independently.
projects.problems: Training organisations faced practical equipment constraints: limited access to real vehicles for mechanics’ workshops, the need to promote training at trade fairs in an engaging way, and a requirement to teach construction standards without on-site risks. VR offered a technical solution to each challenge.
projects.context: Worked at an Annecy-based studio specialising in immersive experiences. Developed three educational XR applications and an internal tool that automated CAD model import tests.
projects.role: Lead developer — independently delivered two of the three applications from design through deployment
highlights: Adapted applications to user feedback and the specific constraints of each deployment environment
Solved real-world constraints with technical solutions, such as replacing unavailable vehicles with VR simulation
Delivered one project across both PC and VR
Created an internal tool to automate CAD model import testing

subProjects.title: Hydrogen training promotion
subProjects.description: An interactive VR application designed to promote hydrogen standards training at trade fairs and make the course more engaging through a playful experience.

subProjects.title: Mechanics workshop
subProjects.description: A VR practical-training module for a mechanics school with limited access to real vehicles. VR made it possible to simulate exercises that could not be performed in real conditions.

subProjects.title: Construction trades
subProjects.description: A cross-platform educational application for PC and VR covering construction trades such as electrical work, industry standards and plan reading.

projects.title: StorySparkle
projects.subtitle: AI-powered story generator
projects.description: An application that generates unique stories from an image uploaded by the user.
projects.problems: Parents do not always have the inspiration to create captivating stories for their children. The idea was to use AI to turn any image into the starting point for a personalised story.
projects.context: A training-course project in which the user uploads an image, the AI analyses it and generates an original story. Stories are saved and can be browsed in a catalogue.
highlights: Integrated the OpenAI API to generate text from images
Built a Flask back end with a PostgreSQL database
Containerised the application with Docker for deployment

projects.title: GameSync

projects.problems: Gamers often struggle to find compatible teammates who share their games, schedules and skill level. Existing platforms do not offer sufficiently precise filtering for these criteria.
projects.context: A project completed during the Web and Mobile Web Developer programme. The full website includes registration, user profiles and a matchmaking system.
highlights: Developed the full stack in vanilla PHP with a MySQL database
Implemented authentication and user-profile management
Built search and matchmaking interfaces

projects.title: RGAAudit
projects.subtitle: Creator & Full-stack Developer
projects.description: An open-source web accessibility auditing tool based on the French RGAA 4.1 standard. It automates the checks that can be automated (around 30–50% of the criteria) and gives human auditors structured data for efficiently completing the remaining manual checks.
projects.problems: In France, RGAA audits are performed manually by specialist firms and are expensive and time-consuming. No open-source tool existed to generate a structured pre-report based on the RGAA grid, make the RGAA ↔ WCAG ↔ audit-engine mapping transparent and auditable, and provide the appendices required for manual verification.
projects.context: A personal project born from a real need in the French digital-accessibility ecosystem. It is local-first, so no data leaves the machine, and open source, with an architecture designed for a future Tauri desktop distribution.
projects.role: Sole designer and developer — from technical specification to implementation
highlights: Designed an npm-workspaces monorepo (core / server / web / cli) ready for Tauri compatibility
Decoupled the axe-core audit engine through an adapter pattern so it can be replaced without changing the rest of the application
Stored the transparent, auditable RGAA ↔ WCAG ↔ axe-core mapping in a versioned JSON file
Implemented automatic discovery through sitemap.xml and recursive crawling, with validation and manual page-list editing
Streamed live progress through Server-Sent Events (SSE)
Generated interactive HTML reports with structured appendices for human auditors
Detected third-party accessibility overlays including accessiBe, UserWay and AudioEye

projects.title: Spoony
projects.subtitle: Daily-life mobile app based on spoon theory
projects.description: A daily-life management mobile app based on spoon theory and designed for people living with chronic fatigue. It helps users make decisions that fit their actual energy levels without guilt.
projects.problems: Existing productivity tools are designed to maximise output, which makes them unsuitable — and sometimes guilt-inducing — for disabled people and those living with chronic illness. They treat daily energy as a constant even though it fluctuates and is limited.
projects.context: A personal project designed end to end: product design, 23 WCAG AA wireframes, a hexagonal back-end architecture and a React Native application. The zero-energy state (0🥄) is a first-class concept rather than an edge case and triggers dedicated business behaviour.
projects.role: Sole designer — product design, architecture, back-end and front-end development
highlights: Applied a hexagonal ports-and-adapters architecture, fully decoupling the business domain from Spring Boot
Designed 22 REST endpoints using JSend, JWT refresh tokens and strict email verification
Made 0🥄 a first-class state that automatically postpones every task scheduled for the day
Built an adaptive suggestion engine based on the remaining spoon budget and task importance
Internationalised the back end with translation keys and the front end with react-i18next, allowing content updates without redeployment
Implemented GDPR-compliant account deletion with a complete cascade
Used TDD as living documentation, defining behaviour in tests before implementation

projects.title: Quotes & Invoices Management App
projects.subtitle: Django REST API — Invoicing tool for sole traders
projects.description: A quotes and invoices management application for sole traders, developed as a team during the training programme. It features a Django REST Framework back end with JWT authentication, PDF exports and unit tests. A React front end was developed in parallel as a foundation for the team.
projects.problems: Sole traders do not always have access to simple, independent invoicing tools. The technical challenge was to deliver a robust API with permission management and compliant document exports, as well as a front-end foundation that junior developers could use.
projects.context: A three-person team project completed during the Application Designer and Developer programme. Because experience levels varied significantly, I acted as the informal tech lead: defining the architecture, organising sprints, developing the main modules and supporting my teammates.
projects.role: Informal tech lead — architecture, database modelling, Docker, JWT authentication, client and quote modules, PDF exports, tests, React foundations and pair programming with less-experienced teammates
highlights: Designed the project architecture and database model around Django ORM constraints
Implemented complete JWT authentication: registration, login, refresh, logout and profile
Built the quotes module with PDF export through WeasyPrint
Wrote unit tests for the modules I developed
Configured Docker Compose for the development environment
Established the React front-end foundation with React Router, React Query and an API layer for the team to continue
Supported teammates through pair programming and introductions to Postman, REST APIs and React fundamentals

projects.title: Finol
projects.subtitle: Exploring COBOL in a modern stack
projects.description: A personal project built to explore COBOL in a practical setting. A COBOL program performs financial calculations — loans, insurance contributions, interest and penalties — and is called from a Spring Boot API through ProcessBuilder. A React interface drives the complete workflow.
projects.problems: COBOL remains widespread in banking and insurance, yet few resources show how it integrates with a modern stack. The aim was to work directly with the language’s distinctive syntax — divisions, PIC typing, strict variable declarations and compile-time fixed memory — and understand COBOL as a business-calculation engine decoupled from the application layer.
projects.context: An independent exploratory project. The parallel with a real mainframe environment is explicit: PostgreSQL stands in for DB2 and ProcessBuilder for a CICS call, while the COBOL business logic remains identical.
projects.role: Sole developer, from design through deployment
highlights: Learned COBOL concepts including divisions, PIC typing, EVALUATE and named paragraphs
Built a Java-to-COBOL bridge with ProcessBuilder, passing parameters through stdin and reading results from stdout
Implemented four financial calculations: loan repayments, insurance contributions, compound interest and late-payment penalties
Secured the Spring Boot REST API with JWT
Created a multi-stage Dockerfile that compiles the COBOL binary and builds the Spring Boot JAR in one image
Built a React interface for creating operations and triggering calculations
